lines.text: Deploying a REST API is easy. But what about handling real-time WebSockets, or building AI agents that actually live inside the conversation? Real-time vendors are expensive — and most AI chat tools bolt agents on as a separate feature.
There's a better way. That's why I built FluxyChat — an open-source realtime platform where chat and AI agents share the same timeline, with tool calls you can actually see.
Powered by Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, and D1 — globally distributed infrastructure. Self-hostable on your own account, or hosted by us in seconds.
Use our SDK and hooks to wire your client in minutes. Then manage everything from a dedicated console. Let me show you how it works.
Scaffold a project with one command. Real terminal, real output — a working chat app in seconds.
Open two tabs. Message in one — it appears instantly in the other. That's edge-native WebSockets, no polling hacks.
Now the part nobody else has. Type at-assistant, ask it to do something — the agent responds in the same timeline, and you see every tool call right there. Not hidden in a log. Not a separate DM.
Operator console for rooms, agents, and billing. Self-host on Cloudflare, or go hosted — your choice.
FluxyChat is in open beta. MIT licensed. Try it at fluxychat.com.
